meta.what: The exclusion and intensity rules of EU Regulation 2020/1818 for Paris-aligned Benchmarks, applied by us to the S&P 500.
meta.regulation_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/1818 of 17 July 2020 supplementing Regulation (EU) 2016/1011 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards minimum standards for EU Climate Transition Benchmarks and EU Paris-aligned Benchmarks
meta.not_a_registered_benchmark_reason: No administrator, no authorisation, no annual review, and our intensity is Scope 1 only where the regulation asks for Scope 1, 2 and 3.

headline.tracking_error_note: 90% block bootstrap on five years of weekly returns, weights held fixed at inception.
headline.reallocation_note: Share of the intensity cut that comes from moving weight between sectors rather than from companies cutting emissions.

meta.intensity_definition: Article 1(c): absolute Scope 1 GHG emissions divided by EVIC in millions. EVIC is market cap plus book total debt; preferred stock and non-controlling interests are not in the SEC tags we pulled.
meta.scope_note: Articles 9 and 11 ask for Scope 1, 2 and 3. We carry mandatory Scope 1 only, for 139 of the 499, and apply it identically to the index and to the universe, so the ratio is like for like and the level is not comparable to a commercial PAB.
meta.cut_note: The cut is measured against the same universe on the same Scope 1 numbers. Exclusions on their own give 70.1%; the figure above is after the Article 3 sector floor puts the weight back into high impact sectors.
meta.overlap_note: 6 companies are barred by more than one article, so the per article counts add to 73 while 67 companies are barred.

paris_score.definition: Rank of a company's Scope 1 intensity inside its own GICS sector. 100 is the lowest intensity in the sector, 1 the highest. A company barred by Article 12 scores 0. A company that files no tonnage and carries its sector's median scores null.
paris_score.bound_note: A company under the US mandatory reporting threshold is ranked on that threshold over its enterprise value, which is a ceiling on its real intensity.
paris_score.reference_note: The ranking runs against every company in the sector that has a number, barred ones included, so the scale is the sector's real spread.

rules.label: Makers of cluster munitions, landmines and other banned weapons.
rules.quote: (a) companies involved in any activities related to controversial weapons

rules.label: Tobacco growers and manufacturers.
rules.quote: (b) companies involved in the cultivation and production of tobacco

rules.label: Companies found in breach of the UN Global Compact or the OECD guidelines for multinationals.
rules.quote: (c) companies that benchmark administrators find in violation of the United Nations Global Compact (UNGC) principles or the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises

rules.label: Coal. Barred at 1% of revenue.
rules.quote: (d) companies that derive 1 % or more of their revenues from exploration, mining, extraction, distribution or refining of hard coal and lignite

rules.label: Oil fuels. Barred at 10% of revenue.
rules.quote: (e) companies that derive 10 % or more of their revenues from the exploration, extraction, distribution or refining of oil fuels

rules.label: Gaseous fuels. Barred at 50% of revenue.
rules.quote: (f) companies that derive 50 % or more of their revenues from the exploration, extraction, manufacturing or distribution of gaseous fuels

rules.label: Power generation above 100 gCO2e per kWh, at 50% of revenue. Both legs have to hold.
rules.quote: (g) companies that derive 50 % or more of their revenues from electricity generation with a GHG intensity of more than 100 g CO2 e/kWh

rules.label: Companies that do significant harm to an EU Taxonomy environmental objective.
rules.quote: companies that are found or estimated by them or by external data providers to significantly harm one or more of the environmental objectives referred to in Article 9 of Regulation (EU) 2020/852
